sections.title: Advanced Concept of Number Series
sections.content: Level 3 transitions into 'Wrong Number Series' and highly complex logic. Here, the patterns involve triple differences, shifting decimals, Fibonacci combinations, and completely illogical/visual reasoning patterns.

sections.title: Wrong Number Series
sections.content: Instead of finding the missing number, you are given a complete series where one number violates the pattern. The difficulty lies in the fact that one wrong number creates TWO wrong differences, throwing off your entire calculation.

sections.title: Fibonacci & Custom Combinations
sections.content: The next term is the sum of the previous two (or three) terms. Sometimes it's the sum of the previous two terms plus a constant. Example: 2, 3, 6, 11, 20 (where 3=2+1, 6=3+2+1, 11=6+3+2).

sections.title: Fractional and Step-Division Series
sections.content: The series grows smaller or fluctuates based on division by increasing numbers, or multiplying by shifting fractions (e.g., x 1/2, x 2/3, x 3/4).

sections.title: Digital Sum / Miscellaneous Patterns
sections.content: These are 'illogical' series where mathematical operations are applied to the digits of the numbers themselves, rather than the whole number. Example: 23, 28, 38, 49 (where the gap is the sum of the digits of the previous number).

sections.title: Prime Gaps and Nested Primes
sections.content: The differences between the numbers are not just primes, but consecutive primes, or the square of primes (4, 9, 25, 49, 121).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. In Wrong Number Series, assuming the number *causing* the weird gap is wrong, rather than checking both sides. 2. Overthinking a simple digital sum pattern as a complex decimal multiplication. 3. Wasting too much time on a single miscellaneous logic question.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 is about speed, pattern recognition, and knowing when to skip. In Wrong Number series, anchor your pattern on the extreme ends. Always keep an eye out for Fibonacci combinations and digit-based operations when standard math fails.

tricks.title: Wrong Number 'Anchor' Trick
tricks.explanation: In a wrong number series, one wrong term produces TWO wrong differences. Start finding the pattern from the side of the series that looks continuous and logical, anchoring your rule there.
tricks.example: Series: 2, 4, 10, 22, 42, 70. Gaps: 2, 6, 12, 20, 28. Gaps 2, 6, 12, 20 follow (1²+1, 2²+2...). The 28 gap is wrong, it should be 30. Hence, 70 is the wrong number.

tricks.title: The Fibonacci Check
tricks.explanation: If the series starts slow, doesn't follow double difference, and multiplication fails, add the first two terms to see if they make the third.

tricks.title: Digital Sum Trap Identifier
tricks.explanation: If a series has large random-looking numbers (e.g., 3-digit numbers) but grows very slowly and difference makes no sense, add the digits of the numbers.

tricks.title: Decimal Multiplication Check (x1.5, x2.5)
tricks.explanation: In advanced series, if the last digits end in 5 or 0 and the growth is aggressive, test x1.5, x2.5, x3.5.

tricks.title: Prime Squares Gap
tricks.explanation: If gaps are 4, 9, 25, 49... do NOT assume the next gap is 81 (9²). Notice that 2, 3, 5, 7 are primes. The next gap is 11² = 121.
